chapter: Hightower: New Orleans parades and early players
title: Roy Palmer's uptown New Orleans work
summary: Palmer lived and worked uptown, where his contacts gave Hightower's band its best early work.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Oh, I was going to ask you, in New Orleans, I don't want to keep you in any longer because everybody wants to get to bed. Roy Palmer, where did he live? Near you, up at 6th Street, around? No, he stayed up Protection Levy.
Way up around Carlton. Around Carlton, the other side of St. Charles.
So maybe he moved down to your neighborhood? No, never did he.

He stayed up in that part of the country, up in that part of the city. Because most of the work that he got was two long grounds that we worked at up there. That's the one that helped us a lot. He knew the people up there, see? And after we got straightened out and, as I told you, could play, that's where we made our greatest reputation up there. Because then most of the time, I hadn't come down to the district where I met Wade Whaley and we had to sign it. We was using Bechet up there, there, see? Oh, yeah. And we had to put long pants in here for him to use him up there, because Bechet was in short pants still. But outside of that, Roy never did come downtown. He never did stay down.
